title: Science‑Backed Benefits of NMN Powder - Health Benefits
abstract:
## Natural Sources of NMN  
NMN is naturally present in the food supply, albeit in tiny amounts. Fruits and vegetables like **edamame, broccoli, cabbage, avocado, cucumber, and tomatoes** contain NMN, as do raw beef and shrimp. ([25](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7238909/#:~:text=recognized%20that%20NMN%20is%20a,plasma%20and%20cerebrospinal%20fluid%20in)) ([26](https://purovitalis.com/foods-that-contain-nicotinamide-mononucleotide-nmn/?srsltid=AfmBOorLO39UvA4SD0abt0UxI_CHxK9KrANjhtu2clxssvIVIvHJGVJa#:~:text=Purovitalis%20purovitalis,tomatoes%2C%20raw%20beef%2C%20and%20shrimp))  
For example, 100 grams of edamame (green soybeans) or broccoli might only provide around 0.5–1.5 mg of NMN – which is a very small dose compared to what supplements provide. Thus, while a healthy diet contributes to NAD+ precursors, **getting meaningful NMN amounts from food alone is difficult**. Most people interested in NMN turn to supplements to achieve the doses used in research (which are hundreds of milligrams).  
**NMN supplements** come in a few forms:  
- **Capsules/Tablets:**Pre-measured doses (125 mg, 250 mg, etc.) of NMN powder in pill form. These are convenient and protect NMN from light and moisture.
- **Bulk Powder:**Loose NMN powder that can be measured with a scoop. Some people mix it into water or juice. The powder has a slightly bitter, vitamin-like taste.
All forms ultimately aim to raise NAD+ levels, but they may differ in speed or efficiency of absorption. For instance, sublingual NMN could theoretically avoid first-pass metabolism in the liver, delivering NMN directly to the blood. ([27](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10917541/#:~:text=introduction%20of%20NMN%20into%20the,this%20is%20the%20best%20and)) However, **no human studies have definitively shown that sublingual is superior** to regular oral dosing– it remains a theoretical advantage. ([27](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10917541/#:~:text=introduction%20of%20NMN%20into%20the,this%20is%20the%20best%20and)) Most of the published research on NMN used standard oral capsules or powders swallowed by mouth, which have been shown to effectively raise NAD+ in blood and muscle. ([28](https://novoslabs.com/frequently-asked-questions/nmn-nicotinamide-mononucleotide/nnm-is-known-to-have-oral-delivery-issues-how-do-you-deal-with-that/?srsltid=AfmBOopetteWjU_vWeWTpO0t4Tizrnp_tWMMTQd91oLmcE0pUkLLxYlH#:~:text=NOVOS%20novoslabs,absorption%20at%20a%20cellular%20level)) ([29](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10721522/#:~:text=clinical%20trials%20evaluated%20the%20safety,NMN%2C%20NAAD%2C%20NR%2C%20nicotinic%20acid)) ([30](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10721522/#:~:text=recent%20investigation%20examined%20the%20safety,most%20selected%20participants%20were%20older))
## Conclusion  
Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) powder represents an exciting development in the science of aging and wellness. As a direct precursor to NAD+, NMN helps replenish a molecule that is indispensable for energy production, DNA repair, and cellular resilience. Research to date – spanning from test tubes to animal models, and now an increasing number of human trials – indicates that NMN supplementation can **raise NAD+ levels** and potentially bring a host of health benefits. These benefits include improved metabolism and insulin sensitivity, better cardiovascular and muscle function, robust neuroprotection, and broad anti-aging effects like reduced oxidative stress and inflammation.
